interface.title: Cell Painting Shortcut Audit — "Does a Cell Painting model see more than a cell count?"
interface.field: Toxicology / high-content imaging (Cell Painting morphological profiling)
interface.stage_of_work: Reading and checking results after analysis, plus planning the next study
interface.what_it_is_for: Lets a toxicologist go through 405 ToxCast/Tox21 endpoints and see where a Cell Painting morphology model has a certified advantage over a cell-count-only baseline after correcting for multiple tests. It also covers calibration, per-compound predictions, enrichment by assay family, example images and sample-size planning for an organ-on-chip study.

data.note: All results are precomputed and ship with the app: Ewald et al. 2026 Cell Painting data on 1,085 compounds, CellProfiler features, allpod aggregation. The audit table (audit_table.csv, about 378 KB, every endpoint with all statistics) downloaded from the All results tab. Microscopy images come from the Cell Painting Gallery (cpg0037-oasis, cpg0036-EU-OS-bioactives). Nothing was uploaded.

features.name: Verdict dot-grid map linked to a detail panel
features.general: A grid of one dot per readout, coloured by category, with a tally legend. Hovering shows a summary, and clicking opens the readout in a detail panel. A search dropdown does the same, and the chosen readout is ringed on the grid.
features.specific: Endpoint plate-map coloured by verdict (advantage, no advantage, indeterminate, positive control). Hovering shows the endpoint name and change in AUROC. Clicking a dot fills the Endpoints tab, and the type-to-search Endpoint box moves the ring on the map.
steps: scan dot colours and the tally legend
hover a dot for its name and delta
click the dot (or type in the search box)
read the opened detail panel; the ring marks the current endpoint
serves_tasks: Scan every readout's verdict at once and pick one to inspect
Check whether the full-profile model beats the simple viability baseline after multiple-testing correction

features.name: Model-comparison verdict card with collapsible statistics
features.general: For one readout, a plain-language verdict, a bar chart comparing several models' scores and an expandable table of test statistics (difference, CI, z, calibrated p, FDR q, minimum detectable effect)
features.specific: Endpoint verdict sentence, 'Ranking accuracy by model' AUROC bars (full morphology, morphology plus cell count, cell-count curve, single cell-count number) and 'Statistics for this endpoint' (bootstrap CI, calibrated and raw p, BH-FDR q, 80%-power detectable effect, logistic sanity check)
steps: select an endpoint
read the verdict badge and sentence
compare the AUROC bars
expand Statistics to read CI, p, q and detectable effect
serves_tasks: Check whether the full-profile model beats the simple viability baseline after multiple-testing correction

features.name: Reliability diagram with calibration metrics
features.general: Plot predicted probability against observed frequency, with a diagonal reference and per-bin hover counts, plus Brier score, ECE and calibration slope
features.specific: 'Do probabilities match reality?' chart for the selected endpoint, with Brier, expected calibration error and slope in the caption. Hovering a point shows the bin and number of compounds.
steps: select an endpoint
compare the curve with the dashed 'perfectly calibrated' line
hover a bin to see how many compounds it holds
read Brier, ECE and slope
serves_tasks: Check whether predicted probabilities match observed frequencies

features.name: Compound lookup with dose-response plot and filterable prediction table
features.general: Search one tested compound, see hit badges and multi-readout concentration-response curves (series toggled from the legend), then a table of each model's predicted probability per readout that can be filtered by category, sorted and searched
features.specific: Compounds tab: type-to-search compound, hit badges (cell count, MT, LDH, Cell Painting), 'Readouts across 8 concentrations' plot, and a 'What the models predicted' table with verdict filter pills and P(active) bars for the morphology and cell-count models
steps: type a compound name and pick it
read hit badges and dose-response lines; hide a series via the legend
toggle verdict pills to filter endpoints
sort by a probability column or search the table
serves_tasks: Find a tested compound and view its concentration-response readouts
Compare measured outcome with each model's predicted probability across readouts

features.name: Two-model score scatter with filterable results table and full-table export
features.general: Scatter of method A vs method B score per readout, with a diagonal and hover details, plus filter pills that narrow the on-screen results table. A separate button exports the complete table, ignoring the filters.
features.specific: All results: full-morphology AUROC against cell-count AUROC scatter coloured by verdict. Category and Verdict pills filter the displayed audit table ('41 of 405 endpoints shown'); 'Download the audit table (CSV)' always exports all 405 endpoints.
steps: hover points to read per-endpoint statistics
toggle Category and Verdict pills
read the filtered table
download the full CSV (filters not applied)
serves_tasks: Compare the two models' scores for every readout and filter the list

features.name: Group enrichment test with switchable baseline and grouping
features.general: Test whether 'wins' are over-represented in any group (Fisher plus cluster permutation, BH-adjusted), switching which baseline defines a win and which attribute defines groups, with a summary callout
features.specific: Where morphology wins: 'Certified advantage measured against' toggle (Cell-count curve / Single cell-count number) and a 'Group endpoints by' dropdown (assay_design_type, assay_mode, assay_target_family, category, cell_short_name, tissue). Shows an odds-ratio and p-value table and an 'enriched or not' callout.
steps: choose the baseline
choose a grouping attribute
read odds ratios and p-values
read the enriched-or-not callout
serves_tasks: Test whether wins cluster in particular groups

features.name: Robustness table across analysis configurations
features.general: One table with a row per analysis configuration (input representation and aggregation rule) giving the count of certified wins against each baseline, so a reader can see whether the headline result depends on those choices
features.specific: Where morphology wins: 'Does the answer survive other choices?' lists certified-advantage counts for each image representation and aggregation rule (e.g. cellprofiler_allpod, cpcnn_allpod, dino_allpod, cellprofiler_all) against the cell-count curve and the single cell-count number

serves_tasks: Check whether the conclusion holds under other feature and aggregation choices

features.name: Sample-size / detectable-effect planner
features.general: Sliders for sample size and positive fraction give a live minimum detectable effect with a typical range, based on a curve fitted to past results. Supporting simulation plots and a table are shown below.
features.specific: Organ-on-chip 'Plan a study': Compounds tested (20 to 400) and Share active (0.10 to 0.50) sliders output 'Smallest advantage over cell count this design can detect' (for example 0.32 → 0.18 → 0.23 AUROC). Below are the 'Simulation across study sizes' figures and table and the grouped-CV boxplot.
steps: set the number of compounds
set the share of actives
read the detectable AUROC and range (help tooltip explains the band)
check against the simulation plots and table

screens_never_reached: Other feature or aggregation configurations (cpcnn_allpod, dino_allpod, cellprofiler_all and others) appear only as rows in the robustness table. The UI has no control to switch the plate-map or Endpoints view to them, so 'MT certified in all three image representations' could not be checked per representation.

The 'Same labels, different cells: HepG2 profiles against primary hepatocytes' section on the Cell lines tab (certified counts in each cell source and both, plus a per-endpoint AUROC scatter). The explorer never scrolled to it.

The All results scatter is display-only: clicking a point did not change the selected endpoint (the plate-map ring stayed on MT, screens/066.webp). Its Category and Verdict filters narrowed the table but not the scatter points (screens/030.webp).

Method tab is static text (screens/058.webp); no controls to try.
